title: Viral Rumor: ISIS Control Tower Takeover

fields.avatarBrief: man in his thirties, beard, wearing a hoodie, casual profile photo
fields.text: THIS IS NOT A DRILL. I just saw a video from inside the terminal. The control tower is under attack by ISIS. Planes are being hijacked and flown into the terminal. I saw a plane crash on the tarmac — it's on fire. People are running. I'm calling 911 now. SHARE THIS BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE.
fields.attachedImageBrief: blurry phone video still showing a darkened terminal hallway with flickering lights and panicked crowd silhouettes

comments.author: Linda R.
comments.text: This is terrifying. I just saw a plane go down on the north side. My cousin works in baggage — he says the FIDS is showing 'crash' for all flights.

comments.author: Marcus T.
comments.text: This has to be fake. The airport is on lockdown. I just saw a police car go by with lights on. But the FIDS says 'Gate B4 now boarding' — that's not possible.

comments.author: Tina K.
comments.text: I'm at Gate B6. Everything's normal here. The FIDS says HW 2401 is on time. No one is running. This post is spreading fear. #StopTheRumor

instructorNote: This is a misinformation inject; the PIO must immediately issue a statement to correct the false claim about aircraft being hijacked or crashed. Watch for the PIO to act before the rumor spreads further.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Emergency Plan (AEP)
citations.headingPath: AEP › Part I › Section 3 › 3.5 Planning Assumptions
citations.quote: - **Notification:** Incidents may occur with little or no warning. Initial notification will likely come from the ATCT or a 911 call. - **Initial Overwhelm:** A significant incident (Alert 3 or Mass C

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Terminal Incident Response Plan (TIRP)
citations.quote: - All Staff: RUN. HIDE. FIGHT.; call 911 or ACC with shooter location/description when safe. - LEO/Security: assume IC; contact teams; establish cold/warm/hot zones; declare scene secure for EMS. - Op

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. A blurry phone video still captured from inside a dimly lit airport terminal hallway. A dark, narrow corridor with cracked linoleum flooring and flickering fluorescent lights overhead. Silhouettes of panicked passengers run in the background, their forms blurred and distorted by motion and low light. One figure in the foreground wears a red airline uniform, turned away, head down, rushing toward the camera. The phone's lens is slightly tilted, showing a corner of a wall-mounted emergency exit sign glowing faintly red. The image has a grainy, overexposed look, with horizontal banding from poor lighting. The background is out of focus, but the sense of chaos and urgency is palpable. Time of day: night, as per terminal lighting. Mood: tense, urgent, disorienting. Setting: inside an airport passenger terminal: check-in counters, rows of dark powered-off departure boards, overhead wayfinding signs seen as plain shapes, luggage carts, high ceilings, large windows
